questions.q: In this lesson's six-step checklist, what comes first, and why?
options: Creating a least-privilege role — access control has to exist before protection or classification mean anything
Sharing the data externally, so partners can start using it immediately
Dropping the table, to test Time Travel before anything else
Running the ACCESS_HISTORY audit query, before any policy exists to audit
questions.explain: The lesson's ordering starts with RBAC deliberately: masking, tagging, and auditing all assume access control is already in place as the foundation.

questions.q: How does this lesson say you prove a masking policy actually fired, rather than just assuming it did?
options: Query ACCESS_HISTORY for policies_referenced IS NOT NULL after running a query that touches the masked column
Check the masking policy's CREATE statement for syntax errors
Ask the user who ran the query whether they saw masked data
There is no way to confirm a masking policy actually evaluated
questions.explain: A non-null policies_referenced value on the relevant query's ACCESS_HISTORY row is real, queryable proof the policy evaluated — not an assumption.

questions.q: Why does step 5 of the lab share through a secure view instead of the raw table?
options: A secure view's masking logic still applies for the consumer, so sharing doesn't bypass the protection built in step 2
Secure views are required by Snowflake for every share, with no exceptions
Raw tables cannot technically be added to a share
Secure views are faster to query than raw tables
questions.explain: This mirrors Lesson 21: sharing a raw table would bypass whatever masking policy protects it, while a secure view carries that protection to the consumer.

questions.q: What is the purpose of step 6 (DROP TABLE, then UNDROP TABLE) in a practice lab rather than a real incident?
options: So the first time you ever run UNDROP is a deliberate, low-stakes test, not your first attempt during a real emergency
To permanently verify a table can never be recovered
To test whether the account has Enterprise Edition
To reset the table's role grants back to default
questions.explain: Practicing UNDROP on a sandbox table builds confidence and familiarity with the real recovery mechanism before you ever need it under pressure.

questions.q: What course does this lesson name as the next step on the Data Governance career path?
options: Power BI Governance
Advanced Databricks
Azure Fundamentals
There is no next course — this is the final course in the path
questions.explain: The lesson closes by naming Power BI Governance as the next course in the Data Governance path, applying the same governance discipline to the BI layer.
